extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians specializing in arithmetic geometry, anabelian geometry, and Inter-Universal Teichmüller (IUT) theory
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts and states structural properties, functorialities, and symmetry/indeterminacy phenomena for D-ΘNF-Hodge theaters, D-NF-bridges, D-Θ-bridges, capsules, and processions in the context of Mochizuki's IUT framework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Base-NF-Bridges functor and F_l-symmetry
rubrics_metrics.description: The operation of associating to a D-ΘNF-Hodge theater the underlying D-NF-bridge determines a natural functor from the category of D-ΘNF-Hodge theaters and isomorphisms to the category of D-NF-bridges and isomorphisms; whose output data admits an F_l-symmetry which acts simply transitively on the index set [i.e., 'J'] of the underlying capsule of D-prime-strips of this output data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a 'forgetful' functor (forgetting Θ-data) whose outputs carry an Fl-torsor symmetry acting simply transitively on the capsule index set; use this symmetry when comparing labeled data that retain the cyclic/F_l-structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Holomorphic Capsules functor and S_l-symmetry
rubrics_metrics.description: The operation of associating to a D-ΘNF-Hodge theater the underlying capsule of D-prime-strips determines a natural functor to the category of l_2-capsules of D-prime-strips and capsule-full poly-isomorphisms; whose output data admits an S_l-symmetry (the symmetric group on l letters) which acts transitively on the index set of this output data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This functor may be thought of as forgetting the labels ∈ F_l; in particular, if one is only given this output data up to isomorphism, then there are precisely l possibilities for the element ∈ F_l to which a given index j ∈ J corresponds prior to applying the functor. Use the S_l action to 'forget the cyclic structure' and to perform absolute comparisons across unrelated capsules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mono-analytic Capsules functor
rubrics_metrics.description: By composing the holomorphic-capsules functor with the mono-analyticization operation (Definition 4.1(iv)), one obtains a natural functor to the category of l_2-capsules of D_4-prime-strips and capsule-full poly-isomorphisms whose output data satisfies the same symmetry properties with respect to labels as the holomorphic-capsules functor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine mono-analyticization with the forgetful capsule functor to obtain mono-analytic cores while preserving the same label-symmetry behavior (useful for forming mono-analytic invariants).

rubrics_metrics.name: Functorial algorithm constructing D-ΘNF-Hodge theater from D-NF-bridge
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a D-NF-bridge, there exists a [relatively simple — cf. discussion of Examples 4.4, 4.5] functorial algorithm for constructing, up to an F_l-indeterminacy, from the given D-NF-bridge a D-ΘNF-Hodge theater whose underlying D-NF-bridge is the given D-NF-bridge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides a constructive (functorial) method to 'lift' a D-NF-bridge to a full D-ΘNF-Hodge theater; expect an unavoidable F_l indeterminacy (torsor) in the output and account for it in comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-labeled output data enable comparison of arithmetic log-volumes
rubrics_metrics.description: The non-labeled output data of the functors of Proposition 4.9 (i),(ii),(iii) allow one to consider isomorphisms between D-prime-strips that were originally assigned different labels, and thus make possible the comparison of objects (e.g., log-volumes) constructed relative to different labels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When computing global arithmetic degrees (log-volumes) of arithmetic line bundles built from étale-theta values, work with the non-labeled outputs of the forgetful functors to compare across labelings; processions can minimize label indeterminacy during such comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Difference between F_l-symmetry (cyclic structure) and S_l-symmetry (full symmetry)
rubrics_metrics.description: Restricting to the F_l-symmetry amounts to imposing a 'cyclic structure' on the index set J (i.e., an F_l-torsor structure); this allows comparisons between distinct members of J without disturbing the cyclic structure. To compare D-prime-strips 'in the absolute' to strips unrelated to J, one must 'forget the cyclic structure' by working with the full S_l-symmetry (i.e., the holomorphic/mono-analytic forgetful functors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose F_l-symmetry for comparisons that must preserve a cyclic combinatorial structure tied to a global D_NF object; choose S_l when absolute, cross-family comparisons are needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Synchronization (cohesion) of labels and necessity for bijection ζ
rubrics_metrics.description: Elements of the index set of the capsule of D-prime-strips of a D-NF-bridge are synchronized in their correspondence with labels '1,2,...,l' in the sense that this correspondence is completely determined up to composition with the action of an element of F_l; this correspondence is always bijective. Nonsynchronized labels (independent F_l- or S_l-indeterminacies at each index) may lead to correspondences that fail to be bijective and are incompatible with the construction of the crucial bijection ζ of Proposition 4.7(iii).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain synchronized (globally coherent) label assignments (bijective up to F_l) when constructing or comparing objects that depend on the bijection ζ; avoid allowing independent local indeterminacies that break bijectivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Synchronized indeterminacy models holomorphic structure; nonsynchronized models real-analytic
rubrics_metrics.description: The synchronized indeterminacy exhibited by a D-NF-bridge (e.g., the bijection ζ) may be thought of as a combinatorial model of a 'holomorphic structure', while nonsynchronized indeterminacies correspond to a combinatorial model of a 'real analytic structure'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the synchronized/F_l-bijective viewpoint when the theory requires holomorphic-type rigidity; consider nonsynchronized viewpoints only when modeling real-analytic phenomena, but expect incompatibilities with constructions needing ζ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Main multiplicative combinatorial Teichmüller theory outcomes (a–d)
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) globalizability of labels, independent of local structures; (b) comparability of distinct labels; (c) absolute comparability; (d) minimization of label indeterminacy via processions — summarize the main results of §4.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the target properties that the constructions (functors, processions, mono-analyticization) are designed to achieve; ensure that constructions respect/produce these properties when applying the theory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of an n-procession (Definition 4.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let C be a category and n a positive integer. An n-procession of C is a diagram P1 → P2 → ... → Pn where each Pj is a j-capsule of objects of C and each arrow Pj → Pj+1 denotes the collection of all capsule-full poly-morphisms from Pj to Pj+1. A morphism of processions consists of an order-preserving injection ι:{1,...,n}→{1,...,m} together with a capsule-full poly-morphism Pj→Q_{ι(j)} for each j.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Processions are the combinatorial devices used to organize nested capsule data; morphisms must preserve order and be given by capsule-full polymorphisms at each index.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processions reduce label indeterminacy (Proposition 4.11(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a D-Θ-bridge φΘ : †DJ → †D>, the assignment φΘ ↦ Prc(†DJ) determines a natural functor to the category of processions whose output data satisfies: for each n∈{1,...,l_2}, there are precisely n possibilities for the element ∈ F_l to which a given index of the n-capsule corresponds prior to application of the functor. Consequently, by considering processions (possibly pre-composed with the forgetful functor from D-ΘNF-Hodge theaters), the indeterminacy consisting of (l_2)(l_3) possibilities that arises in Proposition 4.9(ii) is reduced to an indeterminacy consisting of a total of l_2! possibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use processions to dramatically reduce label indeterminacy: instead of an exponential-type indeterminacy (product of possibilities), processions yield a factorial-sized (l_2!) residual indeterminacy, which is far smaller and more manageable for comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mono-analytic Processions preserve indeterminacy properties (Proposition 4.11(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Composing the procession functor with the mono-analyticization operation yields a natural functor to processions of D_4-prime-strips whose output data satisfies the same indeterminacy properties with respect to labels as in the holomorphic procession case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply mono-analyticization after forming processions when one needs mono-analytic cores while keeping the same improved indeterminacy control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Base-ΘNF (D-ΘNF) link via mono-analyticization (Corollary 4.12(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: The composite functor from the category of D-ΘNF-Hodge theaters to the category of D_4-prime-strips obtained by assigning to a D-ΘNF-Hodge theater the mono-analyticization of the D-prime-strip that appears as the codomain of the underlying D-Θ-bridge; the base-ΘNF (D-ΘNF) link from one D-ΘNF-Hodge theater to another is defined to be the full poly-isomorphism between the D_4-prime-strips obtained by applying this functor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the base-ΘNF link as the canonical 'mono-analytic' comparison/isomorphism between D-ΘNF-Hodge theaters; it is the full poly-isomorphism induced by mono-analyticization of the underlying D-Θ-bridge codomain strips.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mono-analytic core invariant for infinite D-ΘNF-linked chains (Corollary 4.12(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: If an infinite chain of D-ΘNF-linked D-ΘNF-Hodge theaters is given, applying the mono-analyticization functor produces a resulting chain of full poly-isomorphisms between D_4-prime-strips whose output data forms a constant invariant (i.e., a mono-analytic core) of the infinite chain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In applications with infinite linked families, the mono-analytic core provides a stable invariant around which other theaters are 'spokes' — useful when analyzing global symmetry or permutation phenomena.

rubrics_metrics.name: Étale-picture admits arbitrary permutation symmetries among spokes (Corollary 4.12(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Viewing each D-ΘNF-Hodge theater of a linked chain as a spoke emanating from the mono-analytic core yields an étale-picture diagram which satisfies the important property of admitting arbitrary permutation symmetries among the spokes (labels n∈Z of the theaters).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exploit arbitrary permutation symmetries among the linked theaters (spokes) when comparing constructions or transporting data around the mono-analytic core; this reflects high symmetry in the global picture.

rubrics_metrics.name: ΘNF-Hodge theaters satisfy same functorial dynamics as base-ΘNF theaters
rubrics_metrics.description: ΘNF-Hodge theaters (defined in §5) are enhancements of the Θ-Hodge theaters of §3 and satisfy the same 'functorial dynamics' as the base-ΘNF-Hodge theaters discussed in §4 (cf. Deﬁnition 5.5(iii), Corollary 5.6, Remark 5.6.1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When extending constructions from base-ΘNF to full ΘNF contexts, carry over the same functorial operations, symmetry analyses, and procession techniques; the same structural results apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group-theoretic reconstruction of arithmetic objects from π1(†D_6) (Example 5.1(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: By applying anabelian results (AbsTopIII Theorem 1.9 via the Θ-approach) to π1(†D_6), one may construct group-theoretically an isomorph of 'F' (denoted M^(7)(†D_6)) equipped with its π1(†D_6)-action, reconstruct field structure, certain profinite groups corresponding to CF_mod, and various pseudo-monoids of coric rational functions; these constructions are functorial and compatible with the π1-actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use π1(†D_6) and the anabelian algorithms to recover arithmetic data (fields, Frobenioids, pseudo-monoids) functorially; these reconstructions underpin later structural claims (coric structures, decomposition groups, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: κ-sol-conjugate synchronization phenomenon
rubrics_metrics.description: The phenomenon that certain poly-actions (e.g., of F_l) on reconstructed objects are well-defined up to πrat/κ-sol-conjugacy indeterminacies, and that under the constructions described the induced poly-action on the 'κ-sol-outer representation' is, in fact, well-defined without conjugacy indeterminacies and moreover equal to the trivial action; this is referred to as κ-sol-conjugate synchronization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize situations where conjugacy indeterminacies collapse (synchronize) to give well-defined trivial actions on outer representations; such synchronization is important for canonical identifications in the theory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence and uniqueness of ∞κ-coric and ∞κ×-coric structures on †F^(7)
rubrics_metrics.description: †F^(7) always admits an ∞κ-coric (respectively, ∞κ×-coric) structure, which is unique up to a uniquely determined isomorphism (i.e., a pseudo-monoid equipped with a continuous action by πrat_1(†D^(7))).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When associating coric structures to Frobenioids reconstructed group-theoretically, expect unique (up to unique iso) ∞κ and ∞κ× coric structures; these canonical structures are used to relate Kummer classes, cohomology limits, and divisorial data.
